transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Redwood Solutions), Maya Singh (OrbitWorks Head Partnerships), Liam O'Neill (OrbitWorks Dir Cloud Eng), Priya Kapoor (Legal Ops), Ben Torres (Sales Ops)

AutoSummary: quick partner pipeline triage; prioritize three deals; legal handoff; run Dedicated micro-benchmark for latency/cost; share co-sell docs

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — excited to run through the pipeline velocity and surface any gating items. Maya, can you kick us off with the top three deals you want us to focus on?
[00:18] Maya: Yeah, absolutely. Uh so at a glance: Deal A is a fintech integration with strict data residency in EU, Deal B is a marketplace partner where latency matters for search re-rank, and Deal C is a pilot with a health vertical customer that will need private deployment.
[00:35] Ben: Quick note, sales ops is pushing Deal A to close in Q4 so timeline is tight.
[00:41] Diego: Awesome. For Deal B latency, do you have target p50/p95 numbers? Is 200ms p95 acceptable or are we aiming lower?
[00:52] Liam: For the search case, p95 needs to be sub 150ms end-to-end, ideally. That's user facing. We can tolerate some backend queuing but overall we need predictable tail latency.
[01:05] Samira: Okay—good. We should consider Redwood Dedicated for that workload because predictable throughput helps hit tail latency SLAs. Diego, we talked about batching earlier; can you explain the tradeoff live?
[01:18] Diego: Sure. So continuous batching helps throughput and cost but adds a bit of queueing latency. With Dedicated we can tune batch window aggressively to keep p95 low. Also prefix caching—KV cache—sorry K V cash, the transcript's gonna say K V cash, but prefix/KV cache will help for repeated contexts in search ranking.
[01:38] Maya: How about EU data residency for Deal A—can Redwood host that in a region for us or do we need a private/VPC install?
[01:46] Alex: Redwood Hosted supports EU region isolation, but if OrbitWorks requires tenancy separation or specific audit controls, Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated with tenancy guarantees is available. We usually surface a compliance pack first.
[02:01] Priya: On that, we need SOC2 evidence and a sample SOW showing data handling and deletion clauses. Also KMS integration requirements—do you support customer-managed keys?
[02:12] Samira: Yes, we support KMS and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs and a sample SOW after the call.
[02:20] Priya: Great. Also need clarity on e-discovery/audit log retention durations.
[02:26] Alex: We can map retention controls and show the Console's audit trail. We'll provide a short doc with retention configs.
[02:34] Liam: On the technical side: for Deal C (health), there may be an air-gapped requirement. Is an on-prem package realistic?
[02:42] Diego: We do offer an on-prem option; it's heavier but feasible. The main questions will be hardware spec, network isolation, and how we manage model updates.
[02:52] Maya: Great — revenue split mechanics: OrbitWorks usually takes a referral cut but for co-sell we want a stronger GTM motion. Thoughts on a standard playbook?
[03:02] Samira: We have a co-sell one-pager and revenue split template we typically use. It outlines lead registration, crediting, and a standard 20/80 split for inbound vs joint-sourced deals, but it's negotiable. We'll share after this call.
[03:18] Ben: Also need to decide on who owns post-sale support and who bills the customer in each scenario — important for renewal math.
[03:25] Alex: Usually Redwood handles runtime support under the Dedicated/Hosted contracts; for on-prem there's an enterprise support addon and we can white label billing conversations.
[03:36] Samira: Let's triage the three deals quickly — Deal A (fintech) risks?
[03:41] Maya: Latency is okay, biggest risk is legal around EU residency and the customer wants a named SOC2 audit firm. Also pricing sensitivity.
[03:50] Samira: Actionable: Priya send inbound SOW template and must-have clauses. Redwood will provide SOC2 docs and sample SOW. We'll also propose a pricing play for fintech with capped compute credits.
[03:59] [timestamps jump]
[04:30] Liam: For the Dedicated micro-benchmark, can you show cost per 1k tokens and a tail latency sample so we can plug into our TCO model?
[04:41] Diego: Yeah I'll run a micro-benchmark comparing Hosted vs Dedicated. I'll sample across typical prompts, long context and short, and provide CSV with p50/p95/p99 and token cost. Expect numbers that reflect batching and KV cache behavior.
[04:57] Maya: What's the expected turnaround for that?
[05:00] Diego: I can run it this week if we agree scope — say 2000 requests across three prompt profiles — and post results by 2026-11-26.
[05:08] Samira: Good. For Deal B we should also map a canary rollout: start Hosted for speed to market then move to Dedicated when traffic justifies it. Any concerns?
[05:17] Liam: That sounds fine. Need to know how seamless model pinning and fallback are—if Dedicated faces capacity issues can we fallback to Hosted without changing client code?
[05:26] Diego: Yes, we have smart routing and fallback policies. Model variants can be pinned in the config and routing rules will fall back to compatible hosted models; there might be small differences in performance but functionally it's seamless.
[05:38] Maya: Competitors we've heard from the customers are CloudAI and ModelServeX, they push simpler billing but less flexible deployment. We should call out Redwood differentiators: predictable tail latency, co-sell ops support, and audit logs.
[05:50] Samira: I'll draft a one-pager focusing on those differentiators and include a quick ROI slide with sample token economics.
[05:57] Priya: Legal question — will Redwood accept OrbitWorks' standard indemnity language, or do we need to use Redwood's?
[06:05] Samira: We generally start with Redwood's template but are open to negotiation on specific clauses. Alex, can you prepare a note on key negotiables?
[06:13] Alex: Yep, will send a short doc.
[06:17] [10:00] Maya: ok last bit — handoff cadence. We prefer 2-week syncs for the first 6 weeks of co-sell activity, then monthly. Also need a shared pipeline spreadsheet accessible to both teams.
[06:32] Ben: We'll share a sheet after this call, include deal stage, next milestone, risk score, owner.
[06:38] Samira: Recap — Redwood to send co-sell one-pager, SOC2/ISO pack, sample SOW, and execute the Dedicated micro-benchmark for Deal A/B. OrbitWorks to share SOW template and set up exec mapping call.
[06:51] Priya: We'll confirm internal approvers for SOW and share them by Friday.
[07:00] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the notes and set the next sync.

Meeting end.
